question: For $$A=\begin{bmatrix}1&2\\0&3\end{bmatrix},\quad B=\begin{bmatrix}2&-1\\1&0\end{bmatrix},\quad C=\begin{bmatrix}1&0\\2&1\end{bmatrix},$$ evaluate $(2A-B)C+BC$ and use the properties of matrix multiplication and scalar multiplication to establish that the result is equal to $2AC$.
explanation:
Evaluation of the Left-Hand Side

First, $$2A=\begin{bmatrix}2&4\\0&6\end{bmatrix}$$ Therefore, $$2A-B=\begin{bmatrix}2&4\\0&6\end{bmatrix}-\begin{bmatrix}2&-1\\1&0\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}0&5\\-1&6\end{bmatrix}$$ Hence, $$(2A-B)C=\begin{bmatrix}0&5\\-1&6\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}1&0\\2&1\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}10&5\\11&6\end{bmatrix}$$ Also, $$BC=\begin{bmatrix}2&-1\\1&0\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}1&0\\2&1\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}0&-1\\1&0\end{bmatrix}$$ Thus, $$(2A-B)C+BC=\begin{bmatrix}10&5\\11&6\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}0&-1\\1&0\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}10&4\\12&6\end{bmatrix}$$

Use of Matrix Properties

Using the distributive property, $$(2A-B)C+BC=2AC-BC+BC=2AC$$ since $-BC+BC=O$. Directly, $$AC=\begin{bmatrix}1&2\\0&3\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}1&0\\2&1\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}5&2\\6&3\end{bmatrix}$$ Therefore, $$2AC=\begin{bmatrix}10&4\\12&6\end{bmatrix}$$ which agrees with the value already obtained. Hence, $$(2A-B)C+BC=2AC$$ is established.
